subject: design-technology
title: Vacuum Forming a Plastic Shell
objectives: Describe the vacuum-forming cycle in order: clamp, heat, form, cool, release and trim
Explain why the vacuum only removes air and unopposed outside air pressure pushes the pliable sheet onto the mould
Use the outside pressure value, about 100,000 pascals on every square metre, to explain the size of the forming force

definitions.meaning: A forming process in which a heated pliable thermoplastic sheet is pushed onto a mould by outside air pressure after the air beneath it is removed.
The flat plastic sheet clamped in the frame; it softens when heated and sets rigid again when cooled.
The shaped former on the machine bed that rises into the soft sheet and gives the shell its final shape.
The frame that grips the edges of the flat sheet and holds it above the mould through the cycle.
The panel overhead that warms the clamped sheet until the plastic is pliable and sags.
The near-empty space left beneath the sheet when the pump removes the trapped air; it cannot pull on the sheet.
The pressure of the air outside, about 100,000 pascals on every square metre, which pushes the sheet onto the mould once it is unopposed.
The heated sheet after scene 2: softened and sagging, ready to be formed onto the mould.
The cooled formed sheet after scene 4: set rigid, lifted off the mould and trimmed into the finished shell.

mechanismSteps: Setup, sheet clamped: a flat thermoplastic sheet is clamped in a frame above the mould, and the mould rises toward it to start the cycle (s1).
Heating, sheet pliable: the heater warms the sheet until it softens and sags under its own weight, ready to be formed (s2).
Forming, pressure pushes: the mould rises into the soft sheet, the vacuum removes the air trapped beneath it, and unopposed outside air pressure pushes the sheet onto every surface of the mould (s3).
Cooling and release, rigid shell: the formed sheet cools on the mould, sets rigid, and is lifted off and trimmed into a finished shell (s4).
workedExample: Work one cycle stage by stage. Step 1 (s1): clamp the flat sheet in the frame above the mould. Step 2 (s2): heat it until it is pliable and sags. Step 3 (s3): the mould rises into the sheet, the pump removes the trapped air beneath, and outside air pressure at about 100,000 pascals on every square metre pushes the sheet onto the mould. Step 4 (s4): cool the sheet until it sets rigid, lift the shell off, and trim the excess edge.

trap.misconception: The vacuum sucks and pulls the soft plastic sheet down onto the mould.
trap.explanation: The slip: A vacuum cannot pull - it only removes air. With the air gone from beneath the sheet, the ordinary air pressure outside, about 100,000 pascals on every square metre, is unopposed and pushes the soft sheet down onto every surface of the mould. Nothing reaches in to grab the plastic; it is the atmosphere doing the pushing. The fix: The flat sheet is clamped in the frame and heated until pliable, the mould rises into the soft sheet, the vacuum then removes the air trapped beneath it, and the unopposed outside air pressure pushes the sheet onto every surface of the mould, where it cools, sets rigid, and is lifted off and trimmed. In class, replay scene 3: freeze on the label outside air pressure pushes and ask what would move the sheet if the air beneath were still there pushing back - nothing would form it; the sheet forms only because removing that air leaves the outside pressure unopposed.
